definition: The rotational partner of linear momentum: a body's moment of inertia times its angular speed, $L = I\omega$, measured in kg m² s⁻¹.
The total angular momentum of a system stays constant unless a resultant external torque acts on it, so if its moment of inertia falls, its angular speed rises.
The kinetic energy a body has because it is spinning, $E_\text{k} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^{2} = \frac{L^{2}}{2I}$; a rolling body has this as well as its translational kinetic energy.
